title: INNER JOIN
learning_outcomes: Describe the main purpose and behavior of inner join.
Apply a small SQLite example involving matching records from two tables and verify the result.
Identify one failure mode, compatibility constraint, or data-integrity concern related to this topic.

content.intro: This lesson covers inner join as part of SQLite’s embedded relational database model. Work through one small example, verify the output, and then connect the result to the listed subtopics from the supplied curriculum.
content.why_it_matters: One-to-many joins can multiply rows and inflate aggregates if the reporting grain is not controlled.
content.task: Create a second example for inner join. Use at least one of these subtopics: Matching records from two tables, Explicit join conditions, Composite join conditions. Predict the result, run it in a local SQLite environment or supported language binding, and document one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Include a minimal reproducible SQL statement or application snippet.
State the expected result before execution and compare it to the observed result.

content_blocks.title: Example: INNER JOIN
content_blocks.code:
WITH people(id, name) AS (VALUES (1, 'Ari'), (2, 'Bea')), tasks(owner_id, title) AS (VALUES (1, 'Read'))
SELECT people.name, tasks.title FROM people LEFT JOIN tasks ON tasks.owner_id = people.id ORDER BY people.id;
